newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Opel to implement new sick pay law.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Opel to implement new sick pay law.

text.p: General Motors' German unit Adam Opel AG said on Monday it planned from November this year to implement a new law aimed at reducing sick payments to workers from the current 100 percent of salary.

Unlike Daimler-Benz AG, however, which is intent on putting the new law into practice from October 1, Opel said in a statement it would first discuss with its works council "the practical application" of the law.
"Opel wants to create a clause in wage contracts that offers the company the cost savings of the new law but avoids loss of income for the workers," it said in a statement.
The new law is designed to allow companies to cut sick payments from 100 percent of salary down to 80 percent.
But Opel said it saw other possibilities of implementing the spirit of the law by examining ways of using "time credits" based on compensatory over-time work and shift arrangements.

Representatives of Germany's IG Metall union said earlier on Monday that worker's at Opel's plant in Bochum would strike on all three shifts tomorrow if managers decided to impose the cuts as envisaged by the new law.
